subject.title: fix(acp): close shared state database on gateway shutdown (#100637)

question: Should maintainers accept this focused ACP shutdown close as the canonical fix after real-path proof, or prefer the broader shared SQLite cache lifecycle direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100827?
rationale: The code path is now plausibly correct, but the permanent owner boundary is a maintainer choice because sibling PRs split between ACP shutdown wiring, event-ledger lifecycle, and process-global SQLite cache close hooks.

options.title: Accept this focused ACP fix after proof
options.body: Keep this PR as the candidate canonical fix once the author adds real ACP shutdown or hot-reload terminal/log proof and the existing requested-changes review is resolved.

options.title: Prefer the broader cache lifecycle PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100827 if maintainers want SQLite cache owners to close themselves at process exit instead of adding per-server shutdown wiring.

options.title: Choose a ledger lifecycle sibling
options.body: Use a sibling PR only if maintainers want `AcpEventLedger` to grow an explicit close contract and that path preserves the bounded-drain and late-handler safety now present here.

recommendation.title: Accept this focused ACP fix after proof
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as the candidate canonical fix once the author adds real ACP shutdown or hot-reload terminal/log proof and the existing requested-changes review is resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the active requested-changes review for the relevant race and has recent ACP/shared-state lifecycle history.
